statement: Phoenician script descends from Proto-Sinaitic/Proto-Canaanite. The conventional "c. 1050 BCE" cutoff for "Phoenician alphabet begins" is an artifact of a gap in the epigraphic record, not a confirmed founding date; the actual process is a gradual post-Proto-Canaanite standardization phase spanning roughly the late 10th-early 9th century BCE, with a fully standardized 22-letter script emerging c. 1000-900 BCE. The oldest securely dated Phoenician inscriptions are from the 10th century BCE.

sources.citation: General epigraphic literature on Proto-Canaanite/Phoenician transition, converging on c. 1000-900 BCE standardization.
